blocks.raw: <Tip>Think of it as core vs. periphery. The center of the Philippines (where most people and buildings are) is Zone 2, Z = 0.4. Only three provinces far from the main fault systems are Zone 1, Z = 0.2: Palawan, Tawi-Tawi, Sulu. Zone 1 is the exception, not the rule. Batanes is in Zone 2 despite being peripheral — its proximity to Taiwan's seismic zone drives higher hazard.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Confusing Zone 1 and Zone 2 as having equal hazard. Zone 2 is TWICE as hazardous (Z = 0.4 vs. 0.2) and covers nearly all of the Philippines.","Thinking Batanes is in Zone 1 because it is a peripheral province. Batanes is in Zone 2 (Z = 0.4) due to proximity to Taiwan's seismic zone. Only THREE provinces are Zone 1: Palawan, Tawi-Tawi, Sulu.","Using Z = 0.3 or 0.5. The NSCP specifies only Z = 0.2 (Zone 1) and Z = 0.4 (Zone 2). No intermediate values.","Assuming the location's population size determines the zone. Zone is determined by seismic hazard, not city importance. Palawan is Zone 1 even though it has populated centers.","Treating spectral accelerations (Ss, S1) as equivleant to Z factors. NSCP 2015 introduced hazard maps, but the LEA tests the 2-zone system with Z = 0.2 and 0.4."]} />
